sections.h2: Where is Tualatin, Oregon, and what does the name mean?
sections.html:
Tualatin is a southwestern suburb of Portland, located mostly in Washington County with a small piece in Clackamas County. It sits just south of Tigard, and the Tualatin River runs along most of its northern boundary.

The city covers roughly 8 square miles; the Census Bureau lists 8.28 square miles of land. The name comes from the river and is a Tualatin-Yamhill word that probably means “lazy” or “sluggish.” A post office spelled “Tualitin” opened on November 5, 1869, and the spelling changed to Tualatin in 1915. The ZIP code is 97062.

Because the city straddles two counties, the first question for any Tualatin seller is which county holds the parcel. That decides who sends the tax bill and which recorder handles the deed.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Tualatin's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Tualatin began as a river crossing and a railroad stop. In the 1850s the settlement was called Galbreath, after Samuel Galbreath, and in 1853 he built the first bridge over the Tualatin River, after which the town was known as Bridgeport. In the 1880s John Sweek platted a town around the new railroad depot and named it Tualatin. The city incorporated in 1913.

Growth came late. The city’s own comprehensive plan shows land area rising from 0.55 square miles in 1956 to 4.80 in 1980, 7.69 in 2000 and 8.31 in 2019. Population was 7,348 in 1980, 22,791 in 2000, 26,054 in 2010 and 27,942 in 2020.

A few older buildings remain downtown: the Sweek House (1858), the Wesch House and Little White House (1890), the Robinson Store (1912) and Tualatin Methodist Church (1926). Several local place names, including Sweek, Hedges, Brown and Byrom, come from donation land claims. Sellers of homes near the old center may want to ask the city whether any historic review applies.

With 45% of homes rented in the 2020 census, many Tualatin sellers are landlords. A rental house with a tenant in place, deferred repairs or a long vacancy can be harder to list than a move-in-ready owner-occupied one.

sections.h2: Which employers and shopping centers drive Tualatin's economy?
sections.html:
Tualatin mixes retail, manufacturing and health care. Bridgeport Village opened in early 2005 and lies mostly in Tualatin. Nyberg Rivers opened in fall 2014 with about 300,000 square feet of retail, restaurant, fitness and entertainment space, and Nyberg Woods sits at the I-5 and Nyberg Road junction.

On the industrial side, a large Lam Research plant on the south side makes tools for semiconductor manufacturing. Knife makers CRKT and KAI USA (owner of Kershaw and Zero Tolerance) are based here, Shun Cutlery has a location, and Oregon Scientific is headquartered in the city. Legacy Meridian Park Hospital is also in Tualatin.

The comprehensive plan calls industrial land a major local and regional employment center. It sets a 100-acre and a 50-acre parcel minimum for the Southwest Tualatin manufacturing district and a 25-acre minimum for the Medical Center district. The city adopted an Economic Opportunities Analysis on August 28, 2023. A house close to these districts can see truck traffic and shift-change commuting, which buyers notice during showings.

sections.h2: What land rules affect a Tualatin house sale?
sections.html:
Floodplain and natural-area rules are the main land constraints, along with the Basalt Creek planning area to the south. The city’s plan defines the floodplain as the area covered by the 1% annual chance (100-year) flood on FEMA maps.

  • Tualatin River frontage. The northern edge of the city follows the river, so parcels there are the ones to check against FEMA maps.
  • Protected natural areas. The Hedges Creek Wetland and the Tonquin Scablands are named as protected environmental areas, and the city adopted its Natural Resource Inventory and Local Wetlands Inventory on July 14, 1997.
  • Basalt Creek. The city adopted the Basalt Creek Concept Plan on April 22, 2019, and a parks plan for the area on August 12, 2024.
  • Housing density. Policy 3.1.1 sets at least 8 dwelling units per net acre citywide and supports duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, cottages and accessory dwelling units.

The density policy is the reason an owner of a larger lot sometimes has more options than a simple sale of the house. A planner can say whether your zone permits an added unit.

sections.h2: Which schools and transit lines serve Tualatin?
sections.html:
The Tigard-Tualatin School District covers most of Tualatin. Within city limits it operates Bridgeport, Byrom and Tualatin elementary schools, Hazelbrook Middle School and Tualatin High School, which opened in 1992. A small section of the city lies in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District, where students usually attend Stafford Primary. Private options include Arbor School of Arts and Sciences (K to 8) and Horizon Christian High School.

Transportation is a selling point. Interstates 5 and 205, Highway 99W and Highway 217 all serve the city. The WES commuter rail stops at Tualatin Station, TriMet runs bus lines 36, 37, 38, 76, 96 and 97, and South Metro Area Regional Transit’s route 2X stops at the Tualatin Park and Ride. The city adopted a new Transportation System Plan on August 11, 2025, and Tualatin Valley Fire and Rescue provides fire and medical service.

sections.h2: How are Tualatin property taxes billed, and what do they pay for?
sections.html:
Washington County bills most Tualatin parcels, and Clackamas County bills the small part of the city inside its borders. Washington County’s 2025 to 2026 statements were due November 17, 2025, February 17, 2026 and May 15, 2026, with a 3% discount for paying in full and 2% for two-thirds.

The county’s 2023 to 2024 release showed where an average tax dollar goes:

  • 16.52 cents to county government
  • 33.04 cents to cities and special districts
  • 47.06 cents to education
  • 3.38 cents to Metro and the Port of Portland

Taxes follow assessed value, which is the lower of real market value or maximum assessed value, and maximum assessed value usually rises no more than 3% a year. Washington County also reports that compression limits operating taxes to $5.00 per $1,000 of real market value for schools and $10.00 per $1,000 for local government. For a Clackamas County parcel, that county’s 2025 to 2026 bills showed an average single-family home at $691,382 real market value and $370,342 taxable value.

sections.h2: Is there a transfer tax when a Tualatin house sells?
sections.html:
A sale of Tualatin property in Washington County carries a county tax of $1 per $1,000 of the selling price. Payment or an exemption claim is due within 15 days of recording.

Oregon law, in ORS 306.815, generally bars cities and counties from taxing the transfer of real property, with exceptions that include a tax in effect on March 31, 1997. The county’s page, not a city rule, sets the Washington County rate, and it lists exemptions for gifts and inheritances, foreclosure deeds and court-ordered transfers. If your parcel is in the Clackamas County sliver, the Washington County page does not apply to it, so ask the title company which rules cover that address.

sections.h2: What are the steps in a cash sale of a Tualatin house?
sections.html:
A cash sale is a direct purchase of the house as it is, closed through a title company. The usual path is a property review, an offer, a signed contract, title work, and a recorded deed.

Oregon’s seller disclosure rules still apply unless an exclusion fits, and the buyer has five business days after delivery of the form to revoke an offer. Ask for the title company’s closing statement ahead of time so you can see the tax proration and transfer tax lines.

faqs.q: Is Tualatin in Washington County or Clackamas County?
faqs.a: Tualatin is mostly in Washington County, with a small portion in Clackamas County. Check your tax statement or the county assessor's record to see which one bills your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Tualatin?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied homes is $628,200. That is a citywide survey figure, not a value for a specific house.

faqs.q: Which school district is Tualatin in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Tigard-Tualatin School District. A small section is in the West Linn-Wilsonville School District.

faqs.q: Does Tualatin have a transfer tax?
faqs.a: For property in Washington County, the county charges $1 per $1,000 of the selling price. Buyer and seller decide who pays it in their contract.

faqs.q: Do I need FEMA flood information to sell a Tualatin house near the river?
faqs.a: It helps. The city's plan uses FEMA maps to define the 100-year floodplain, and a buyer or lender may ask whether the house sits inside it.
